items.stem: What is the safest way to use a GitHub Copilot suggestion in production code?

options.text: Read it, understand it, and cover it with a test before relying on it
options.rationale: Correct: reviewed and tested suggestions are accountable code.

options.text: Accept every suggestion to save time
options.rationale: Blind acceptance ships unreviewed, possibly wrong code.

options.text: Assume generated code needs no tests
options.rationale: Generated code needs the same testing as hand-written code.
Removing tests reduces, not increases, confidence.

items.explanation: Correct: reviewed and tested suggestions are accountable code.

items.stem: Which TWO practices protect an enterprise .NET API? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Require authentication and an authorization check on protected endpoints
options.rationale: Correct: authN/authZ restrict access to permitted callers.

options.text: Keep connection secrets in configuration, not in source
options.rationale: Correct: secrets in source control leak to everyone with repo access.

options.text: Skip validation when the client is internal
options.rationale: Internal clients still send bad or malicious input.

options.text: Hard-code the database password in the controller
options.rationale: Hard-coded secrets are exposed in source history.

items.explanation: Correct: authN/authZ restrict access to permitted callers.

items.stem: Why run the API's tests in CI on every pull request?

options.text: To catch regressions before changes merge
options.rationale: Correct: CI tests gate merges and catch breakage early.

options.text: Because it removes the need for a version policy
options.rationale: Versioning and testing address different concerns.

options.text: Because tests in CI never need maintenance
options.rationale: Tests are maintained like any other code.

items.explanation: Correct: CI tests gate merges and catch breakage early.
